stem: At the end of Matthew's Gospel (28:19, Douay-Rheims), Jesus sends the apostles out to baptize. In whose name, the same words Catholics say with the sign of the cross?
options: the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob
the Lord Jesus Christ, and of his twelve apostles
the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost
the Father, and of Moses, and of all the holy prophets
why: Matthew 28:19: "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." The same Trinitarian words are said at baptism and with the sign of the cross (Catechism 232–233).
source: Matthew 28:19 (Douay-Rheims); Catechism of the Catholic Church 232–233

es.stem: Al final del Evangelio de Mateo (28,19), Jesús envía a los apóstoles a bautizar. ¿En el nombre de quién, con las mismas palabras que dicen los católicos al hacer la señal de la cruz?
options: el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob
el Señor Jesucristo y sus doce apóstoles
el Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo
el Padre, y de Moisés, y de todos los santos profetas
es.why: Mateo 28,19: "bautizándolos en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo". Las mismas palabras trinitarias se dicen en el bautismo y al hacer la señal de la cruz (Catecismo 232–233).

stem: The Council of Trent taught transubstantiation (Catechism 1376). What does the Church mean by it for the bread and wine at Mass?
options: their whole substance becomes Christ's body and blood, while they still look like bread and wine
Christ becomes present beside them, while they stay bread and wine in their substance as well
their look and taste turn into flesh and blood, while underneath they remain bread and wine
they stay just as they were and serve as a holy reminder of the meal Jesus shared at the Last Supper
why: Trent (Session 13, canon 2) and Catechism 1376: by the consecration the whole substance of the bread becomes Christ's body and the whole substance of the wine his blood; the appearances (the look, taste and feel) of bread and wine remain.
source: Council of Trent, Session 13; Catechism of the Catholic Church 1376

es.stem: El Concilio de Trento enseñó la transubstanciación (Catecismo 1376). ¿Qué quiere decir la Iglesia con eso sobre el pan y el vino en la misa?
options: toda su sustancia se vuelve el cuerpo y la sangre de Cristo, aunque sigan pareciendo pan y vino
Cristo se hace presente junto a ellos, mientras siguen siendo pan y vino también en su sustancia
su aspecto y su sabor se vuelven carne y sangre, mientras por debajo siguen siendo pan y vino
quedan tal como estaban y sirven como un recuerdo santo de la cena que Jesús compartió la última noche
es.why: Trento (sesión 13, canon 2) y el Catecismo 1376: por la consagración, toda la sustancia del pan se vuelve el cuerpo de Cristo y toda la sustancia del vino su sangre; las apariencias (el aspecto, el sabor y el tacto) del pan y del vino permanecen.

stem: On the rosary as Catholics commonly pray it, which prayer is said on each of the ten small beads of a decade?
options: the Our Father
the Hail Mary
the Glory Be
the Memorare
why: Each decade is one Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be, while the person meditates on a mystery from the lives of Jesus and Mary (Pius V, Consueverunt Romani Pontifices, 1569; John Paul II, Rosarium Virginis Mariae 33–35).
source: Pius V, Consueverunt Romani Pontifices; John Paul II, Rosarium Virginis Mariae 33–35

es.stem: En el rosario tal como lo rezan comúnmente los católicos, ¿qué oración se dice en cada una de las diez cuentas pequeñas de una decena (un misterio)?
options: el Padre Nuestro
el Ave María
el Gloria
el Acordaos
es.why: Cada decena es un Padre Nuestro, diez Ave Marías y un Gloria, mientras se medita un misterio de la vida de Jesús y de María (Pío V, Consueverunt Romani Pontifices, 1569; Juan Pablo II, Rosarium Virginis Mariae 33–35).

stem: How does the Catechism (1667–1670) set sacramentals, such as holy water or a blessed medal, apart from the seven sacraments?
options: they are signs the Church instituted, which prepare people to receive grace
they are signs Christ instituted, which give grace by the rite performed
they are objects that protect whoever carries them, with or without faith
they are local customs that the Church only puts up with and has never blessed
why: Catechism 1667 and 1670: sacramentals are sacred signs instituted by the Church; they do not give grace the way the sacraments do, but by the Church's prayer they prepare people to receive it. Treating them as working apart from faith is superstition (Catechism 2111).

es.stem: ¿Cómo distingue el Catecismo (1667–1670) los sacramentales, como el agua bendita o una medalla bendecida, de los siete sacramentos?
options: son signos instituidos por la Iglesia, que preparan para recibir la gracia
son signos instituidos por Cristo, que dan la gracia por el rito realizado
son objetos que protegen a quien los lleva, tenga fe o no la tenga
son costumbres locales que la Iglesia tolera pero nunca ha bendecido
es.why: Catecismo 1667 y 1670: los sacramentales son signos sagrados instituidos por la Iglesia; no dan la gracia como los sacramentos, pero por la oración de la Iglesia preparan para recibirla. Tratarlos como si funcionaran sin la fe es superstición (Catecismo 2111).

stem: In Luke 1:38 (Douay-Rheims), Mary answers the angel Gabriel: "be it done to me according to thy word" (in Latin, fiat). What does the Church see in this answer (Catechism 494)?
options: her doubt, for which the angel left her unable to speak
a command she had no real freedom to turn down
her wish to wait for Joseph's word before agreeing
her free consent, in faith, to what God asked of her
why: Catechism 494: giving her consent to God's word, Mary became the mother of Jesus, freely and with her whole heart. (It is Zechariah, not Mary, who is struck mute for doubting, Luke 1:20.)
source: Luke 1:38 (Douay-Rheims); Catechism of the Catholic Church 494

es.stem: En Lucas 1,38, María le responde al ángel Gabriel: "hágase en mí según tu palabra" (en latín, fiat). ¿Qué ve la Iglesia en esta respuesta (Catecismo 494)?
options: su duda, por la que el ángel la dejó sin poder hablar
una orden que ella no tenía libertad real de rechazar
su deseo de esperar la palabra de José antes de aceptar
su libre consentimiento, en la fe, a lo que Dios le pedía
es.why: Catecismo 494: al dar su consentimiento a la palabra de Dios, María llegó a ser la madre de Jesús, libremente y con todo el corazón. (Es Zacarías, no María, quien queda mudo por dudar, Lucas 1,20.)

stem: A family in Lebanon belongs to the Maronite Church, with its own liturgy partly in Syriac. According to the Second Vatican Council (Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3), how is that Church related to the Catholic Church?
options: an Orthodox church outside communion with the pope
a Latin-rite diocese that has a translated Mass
an Eastern Catholic Church in full communion with Rome
a separate church Rome plans to merge into the Latin rite
why: Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3 (Vatican II): the Eastern Catholic Churches, the Maronites among them, keep their own rites and are in full communion with the bishop of Rome, equal in dignity with the Latin Church; catholic means universal (Catechism 830–835).
source: Second Vatican Council, Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3; Catechism of the Catholic Church 830–835

es.stem: Una familia en el Líbano pertenece a la Iglesia maronita, con su propia liturgia en parte en siríaco. Según el Concilio Vaticano II (Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3), ¿cómo se relaciona esa Iglesia con la Iglesia católica?
options: una iglesia ortodoxa fuera de la comunión con el papa
una diócesis de rito latino que tiene la misa traducida
una Iglesia católica oriental en plena comunión con Roma
una iglesia aparte que Roma piensa fusionar con el rito latino
es.why: Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3 (Vaticano II): las Iglesias católicas orientales, entre ellas la maronita, conservan sus propios ritos y están en plena comunión con el obispo de Roma, con igual dignidad que la Iglesia latina; católica quiere decir universal (Catecismo 830–835).

stem: Catholics ask Mary and the saints to pray for them. How does the Church explain the difference between this and the worship given to God?
why: Adoration (worship) belongs to God alone; Mary and the saints receive honor (veneration). Asking them to pray for us is asking for their intercession, as one might ask a fellow believer, because the communion of saints joins Christ's people living and dead (Catechism 956, 971, 2132).

rubric.point: Says worship or adoration belongs to God alone, while Mary and the saints are honored or venerated. Saying only that 'Catholics respect saints' without the contrast with worship counts as partly.
Says that asking a saint is asking them to pray for us (intercession), not asking them to do what only God does. Saying the saints themselves grant the request on their own power does not count.
Mentions the communion of saints, the bond of the living and the dead in Christ, or compares it to asking a friend to pray (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: Los católicos les piden a María y a los santos que recen por ellos. ¿Cómo explica la Iglesia la diferencia entre esto y el culto que se le da a Dios?
es.why: La adoración (el culto) le corresponde solo a Dios; María y los santos reciben honra (veneración). Pedirles que recen por nosotros es pedir su intercesión, como se le pediría a otro creyente, porque la comunión de los santos une al pueblo de Cristo, vivos y difuntos (Catecismo 956, 971, 2132).

stem: According to the Gospels, who first found Jesus' tomb empty on Easter morning, and what were they sent to do?
why: All four Gospels name women, Mary Magdalene among them, as the first at the empty tomb, and they are sent to tell the disciples (Matthew 28:7, Mark 16:7, Luke 24:9, John 20:17–18). In John, Mary Magdalene meets the risen Jesus, and tradition calls her the apostle to the apostles.

rubric.point: Names women, or Mary Magdalene, as the first to find the tomb empty. Naming only Peter or the apostles does not count.
Says they were sent to tell the disciples or apostles that Jesus had risen. 'They told people' without the disciples counts as partly.
Mentions Mary Magdalene meeting the risen Jesus in John's Gospel, or her title 'apostle to the apostles' (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: Según los Evangelios, ¿quiénes encontraron primero vacío el sepulcro de Jesús la mañana de Pascua, y qué se les mandó hacer?
es.why: Los cuatro Evangelios nombran a unas mujeres, entre ellas María Magdalena, como las primeras en llegar al sepulcro vacío, y se les manda avisar a los discípulos (Mateo 28,7; Marcos 16,7; Lucas 24,9; Juan 20,17–18). En Juan, María Magdalena se encuentra con Jesús resucitado, y la tradición la llama apóstol de los apóstoles.
